page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with a dedicated 16-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon W-3235 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. Complementing the CPU subsystem is 84.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.25 GB of RAM per physical core, alongside a bundled 400 GB local SSD and 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Hardware acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs built on the Turing architecture, delivering a cumulative 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM across the three devices. In computational benchmarks, this multi-GPU configuration achieves top-tier results in LLM inference workloads. Prompt processing reaches 1,827.36 tokens per second on 7B models and 220.48 tokens per second on 70B models, while text generation rates place in the top percentiles for small and medium model sizes.

General-purpose computing metrics present a balanced profile. PassMark CPU testing yields 20,742.83, while single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores reach 1,497.0 and 8,980.0 respectively, reflecting middle-tier performance typical of dedicated workstation-class processors. Memory subsystem evaluations reveal strong PassMark memory throughput, though large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is comparatively limited at 25.38 GB/sec.

With 48 GB of aggregated GPU memory distributed across three physical GPUs, OVHcloud rtx5000-84 offers high density for parallelized AI inference, multi-stream video transcoding, 3D graphics rendering, and computer vision pipelines, providing solid compute resources where multi-GPU parallelism can be fully exploited.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server engineered for parallel computing, AI inference, and rendering pipelines. Built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor, it features a dedicated 16-core Intel Xeon W-3235 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz, 84.0 GB of system memory, a 400 GB local SSD, and 10 Gbps network connectivity. Compute acceleration is provided by three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 Turing GPUs offering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results show strong performance in machine learning inference, with top-tier throughput for prompt evaluation and generation across various model architectures. General host processing and memory throughput remain balanced in middle tiers. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for distributed deep learning inference, image processing, 3D rendering workloads, and multi-stream visual analytics.
